caption: A man slips on a wet floor in a supermarket aisle and falls down.

sa.check: A man walks along a supermarket aisle.
He slips on a wet patch of floor.
The floor is visibly wet where he slips.
The slip comes first and the fall follows.

pc.expect: Once his balance goes he comes down to the floor and stays.
pc.fail: He hangs mid-fall; or rises; or bounces back to his feet.

pc.expect: His foot shoots forward, his arms fly up, and his body bends only at the joints.
pc.fail: His body folds mid-torso; or a limb detaches; or his legs pass through each other.

pc.expect: The slip starts where his foot meets the wet patch.
pc.fail: He slips on dry floor away from the patch; or falls before reaching the patch; or his foot slides with no contact.

pc.expect: He lands on the floor, not in it.
pc.fail: He passes into the floor; or passes through a shelf; or a shelf passes through him.

pc.expect: His limbs keep their number and stay attached.
pc.fail: A limb detaches or vanishes; or a second figure appears; or he merges with the shelving.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: His clothing and the aisle stay the same.
pc.fail: His clothing changes colour; or the shelves rearrange; or the wet patch moves.

note: Biomechanics scene: the body is the physics. Gait, posture, style and skill are not judged; only that limbs stay attached, bend at joints, keep ground contact and pass through nothing.
